text:
perf-bot: nightly-alert: 99p latency for kernel-selector path up ~2.1x vs baseline for the 03:00-04:00 UTC window. link: https://dash.internal.redwood/alerts/4415009999

maria: seeing it on the dashboard too, started ~03:12 UTC, affects canary and some prod lanes.
devin: which kernel families are spiking? kernel-selector metrics look noisy.
raj: looks like kernel-choice weight shifted to 'execpath-v2' more often around the deploy. correlating with PR #8521 merge.
elaine: can we confirm the merge? deploy-bot: PR merged by @sophia at 2026-03-18T02:59:48Z -> rollout started 03:00 UTC (canary first).
sophia: that was the kernel-selection heuristic tweak (reduce warm-prefetch threshold, change epsilon). intended to favor lower-latency kernels but maybe backfired on longer seqs.
maria: stack traces/heatmap? I pulled a few 99p traces from canary hosts:```
# sample tail latency trace
kernel=execpath-v2 seq_len=1024 batch=1 cold_kv_miss=true
cpu_ms=18.6 gpu_ms=145.2 kv_lookup_ms=72.3 total_ms=240.1
```
devin: kv_lookup_ms looks high. maybe prefetch policy changed interaction with large sequences -> more KV thrashing.
raj: I ran a quick grep in the canary logs, saw a surge of cache evictions shortly after the rollout: `kv_evictions_count` jumped 3x at 03:14.
elaine: interesting, the heuristic reduced prefetch aggressiveness for small prefixes but might be delaying big-prefix prefetch, causing synchronous KV loads.
sophia: rolling back is an option but let's bisect quickly to confirm causal. I'll trigger a bisect build/offline test to replay representative traces.
maria: also saw an uptick in batching-window shrink events (batcher reduced window) coincident with the kernel switch. that would increase per-request overhead.
devin: test plan: (1) replay a sampled canary traffic subset in CI with and without the PR, (2) run the offline perf harness with exact KV cache sizes, (3) run lightweight bisect on the kernel-selector flow to toggle the epsilon param.
sophia: kicking off replay job now: `ci/replays/4415009999-replay --trace canary-03-12-03-20 --compare pr-8521 main`
perf-bot: replay job queued: run id 77421. expected ~18m.
raj: while that's running, I pushed a debug flag to canary to emit detailed prefetch decisions (`kernel.prefetch.debug=true`) for a single host to avoid noisy logs.
maria: output from the debug host shows repeated prefetched keys evicted before use when `execpath-v2` is chosen for long sequences. snippet:```
[03:13:22] prefetch(keys=128) chosen_kernel=execpath-v2 cache_free=120MB evictions=4
[03:13:22] use(keys=128) cache_hit=false -> sync_kv_fetch
```
devin: that pattern explains the kv_lookup_ms bump. execpath-v2 seems to assume low eviction churn; with reduced prefetch it ends up fetching synchronously.
sophia: replay results: run 77421 shows aggregate 99p latency +110% with pr-8521 vs main. attaching diff: https://ci.internal.redwood/runs/77421/diff
elaine: confirmed. also reproduced locally with `harness --kv-capacity=128MB --seq=1024 --prefetch-mode=adaptive`.
maria: ops question: is this limited to large seq workloads (>=512) or broader?
raj: logs indicate 92% of affected requests had seq >= 512. smaller sequences unaffected.
sophia: options: (A) revert PR #8521 immediately (fast), (B) patch heuristic to re-enable aggressive prefetch for seq >=512, (C) gradual param rollback and targeted canary.
devin: prefer B if low-risk: narrow condition for aggressive prefetch when predicted seq > 512 and cache pressure low. but we need tests.
elaine: for rollout safety, we should hold the release and revert to unblock SLOs for prod traffic. canaries are impacted already.
maria: ops: hold put on the rollout confirmed. I'll set the rollout to paused and notify infra.
sophia: opening revert PR now: #8530 revert PR #8521. patch is minimal.
perf-bot: ci/job 77445 started for revert PR #8530 -> running unit+perf smoke.
devin: in parallel I'll prepare a narrower patch PR that changes prefetch to `if seq_predicted >= 512 then aggressive=true` and add synthetic perf tests.
raj: we should also add a regression test in nightly harness: a trace with repeated long-seq requests and limited KV capacity.
elaine: can we estimate rollback impact? will revert reintroduce prior inefficiency?
sophia: revert returns us to previous, which had stable latency on long seqs. we'll lose the micro-optimizations for small prefixes but restore SLO.
maria: revert CI passed smoke tests, perf smoke shows 99p back to baseline in canary replay. perf-bot: job 77445 completed, status: success.
deploy-bot: revert PR #8530 merged by @maria at 2026-03-18T03:45:12Z. rollout paused -> rolled back canary.
raj: post-rollback monitoring shows 99p going down towards baseline over next 8 minutes.
sophia: creating a follow-up ticket to rework the selection heuristic with stricter gating and a KV-aware feature flag: RD-1129.
devin: assign me and raj, I'll prototype a predictive-prefetch toggle and add unit perf tests.
maria: thanks all. action items: 1) observability: add canary-level KV eviction alerts and regression unit for seq>=512 (elaine), 2) design patch with KV-aware prefetch gating (devin+raj), 3) add replay harness scenario to nightly (sophia), 4) postmortem to be filed if SLO impact > 30mins (maria).
elaine: logging the incident and opening a short incident channel for postmortem notes.
sophia: quick note for release process: avoid heuristic flips without a replay scenario in CI.
maria: closing the thread in 30m unless new regressions appear. :thumbsup:
